reply.instructions: Hydralysis <version>. Twenty-one tools for any PE you own. prepare adopts an analysed project in place, or imports/analyses a new executable exactly once as a durable job, and registers its build; backend discovers/installs the engines, never their MCPs. job reports progress. runtime manages verified debugging/instrumentation sessions. inspect is the function picture (bounds, prologue, instructions, callers) and does not start a JVM. sigscan and prologue are how a hook site is found and checked. ghidra_run runs one of your scripts contained, so it cannot change the project. Prefer ghidra_query for bounded address-based decompilation and references; one warm engine serves CLI, MCP and script clients; export writes bulk artifacts as a job. Addresses there are VAs or explicit rva:/va:. For PE addresses use rva:0x... or va:0x... when the interpretation is ambiguous. trace records and queries what a program did (cited, bounded, with coverage gaps); capture itself is runtime. Do not re-import the binary. evidence_add stores a claim only with a source.

actions.blocks: basic blocks and their observed static edges

data.table: optional bool: bounded pointer candidates at address; inferred vtables require further evidence

actions.decompile/function/functions/xrefs: read-only analysed results with bounded continuation

diff.against_view: optional source annotation view; shared by default
diff.checks: optional source prologue table; destination candidates require independent review, not ready-to-install checks; runs as a job
diff.view: optional destination annotation view; shared by default

export.resume: existing export job id; source/options identity must match

orphans.referenced_only: optional bool: only runs something refers to
orphans.use: decoded code no function contains, with references to each run's start: evidence for type_edit function_create

pcode.nodes: 1..200; stable op/varnode IDs seed a trace

scan.regex: optional case-insensitive regex over MNEMONIC operands; decoded listing, at most 2000 instructions/page; use next_cursor

type.path: exact database category path, or use address for typed data

type_edit.batch: edits=[{address,options}] OR file=JSON array path, 1..200 nonbatch children, atomic; source inherited if absent
type_edit.concurrency: shared view: expect_revision is mandatory and stale edits conflict unless their subjects are untouched. Named views: per-agent isolation (one agent per view name); they are not merged back. Per-agent views by default is deferred until publish/merge exists
type_edit.expect_revision: REQUIRED for every edit and revert, on the shared view and on named views: the view_revision you read (ghidra_query status, or any edit answer). A missing value is an error that names the current revision. A stale one is rebased automatically (answer rebased:true, rebased_from, subjects_changed_since) when no edit after it touched this edit's subject (address, struct path, or function structure); otherwise it is a conflict {conflict, current_revision, latest_editor {by, at}, subjects_changed_since, overlapping, history_complete}. A type import touches every subject. Subjects are addresses and type paths; dependencies between them are not tracked. A view that predates the journal cannot be rebased until you re-read it. An edit refused with stale_view (master_generation_changed: another view published a generation and this view holds records on the older one) recorded nothing and is never retried by Hydralysis: rebase with type_edit kind=rebase (the call in the refusal's next), then send the edit again with the revision the rebase answers
type_edit.function_create/function_body: expect=exact entry bytes, ranges=[{start,end}] numeric inclusive VAs; optional name
type_edit.function_delete: expect=exact entry bytes; explicit entry VA
type_edit.import_archive: archive=absolute .gdt path; source required; paths=[exact type paths] optional. Whole archive requires matching data organization; selected types use strict recursive layout checks. Runs as a job and reverts as one edit
type_edit.import_types: corpus=absolute JSONL path (docs/type-corpus.md), category?; runs as a job; revertible in one step
type_edit.label: name at a mapped address (including data)
type_edit.revert: ids=[overlay ids]: one step; the working copy is rebuilt from the master
type_edit.shape: all options are flat, next to kind: {"kind": "struct", "path": ..., "size": ..., "fields": [...]}, never {"struct": {...}}
type_edit.struct: path, size, fields=[{offset, type, name, length?}]
type_edit.view_revision: every status and edit/revert answer reports it (status: view_revision and overlays.latest_editor); a named-view edit reports sync.phases_ms {master_open, fork, copy (part of fork: the engine's clone/copy time), base_upgrade, open, replay, total}, all whole milliseconds

actions.types: paged types, optional contains and cursor
actions.variables: recovered local/parameter types for address's function

vcalls.receiver_from/receiver_type/receiver_glo: optional: verify each site's receiver on p-code
vcalls.vtable: optional: names the implementation and its direct callers

actions.vtables: address = a function: the tables of code pointers that hold it, and its slot

writes.coverage: direct [reg+offset] stores; the answer lists what it does not cover
writes.receiver_type: optional struct name to verify the store's base

carriers.backend action=backups: options.op = list (default) | verify, plus selectors; lists and re-hashes backups and generations; unfinished candidates are listed, never deleted; not_available until backups ship
carriers.backend action=doctor: read-only health findings [{id, level, what, why, fix}]; options.sections/verbose; not_available until the doctor ships
carriers.ghidra_query options: planned: type_edit kinds commit, commit_revert, rebase, publish, merge, export_bundle, import_bundle (no address needed); status options.show = changes|views|lineage|queue|health; carried by the existing options object, not yet implemented unless listed under actions
carriers.ghidra_run options: {isolation: private|exclusive|worker, readonly: bool}; shared is refused. On an engine that reports scriptIsolation a script on a view runs as worker (the view is saved once if changed and passed as basedOn), on a program as private; readonly:true fails the job when the script attempted changes. On an engine without it, options answer not_available (the script is not run) and no options = the contained mode
carriers.job options: reserved for status/cancel filters of commit and backup jobs (kind, cid); non-empty options answer not_available today
carriers.note: Where later features live. A carrier whose capability is not implemented answers {not_available: <capability>, message} as a result, not an error, and does nothing. The options objects are free-form in the schema.

json.flow_limits: Recovered high-pcode dependencies and direct-call bindings are evidence, not proof of runtime reachability, complete aliasing, or indirect targets.
json.jobs: job status with id returns stage, elapsed time and bounded progress log; job cancel requests owned-process cleanup

option_bags.backend: action=backups options.op (list, verify, remove: remove is a dry run unless confirm:true) and selectors; action=doctor options (sections, verbose)
option_bags.ghidra_query: type_edit options.kind (commit, commit_revert, rebase, publish, merge, export_bundle, import_bundle, plus today's kinds), options.view, options.expect_revision, options.as (the agent identity of the call, D59); status options.show (changes, views, lineage, queue, health)
option_bags.ghidra_run: options.isolation (private, shared, exclusive), options.readonly, options.as (the agent identity of the call, D59)
option_bags.job: status/cancel filters (kind, cid) for commit and backup jobs
option_bags.trace: per-action options: start (profile, images, scope, launch, program), query (kinds, filter, group_by, cursor, up_to, interpretation, profile_query), diff (against, group_by, align), explain (event_id, depth, direction), mark (label, phase), export (name, overwrite), check (assertions), import (input), resymbolize (program), reprocess (codecs, context|contexts, kinds, note), relations (op), evict (to_quota), bundle (path); start also takes meta fields (target, scenario, capture_options, shared_scope); writes use the cap that start returned; offline=true runs import/verify/rebuild/export on files; every action takes limit

json.prepare: action=adopt path=<.gpr, its folder or a parent> exe|sha256 [program] [target]: register an analysed project in place (no copy, no import). action=plan exe: read-only preflight. action=start exe [install=true]: one-time import/analysis job; identical builds reuse one result
json.prologue: Single address/expect or checks[{address,expect,name?}], 1..200 rows, one PE open/hash. CLI --checks-file accepts canonical rows or legacy offset/prologue/names with explicit --offset-kind.
json.queries: ghidra_query uses configured or prepared target, numeric VA or rva:/va:, action, limit/cursor/contains/timeout_s and options. Imported address maps also permit name:<name> and hash:0x<hex>. options.view selects a named annotation view; shared is the default. Views isolate edits, not access control.
json.setup: backend inspect discovers the pinned Hydra Engine, its client and a JDK; backend install starts a private, verified installation job; backend status/stop show or stop the shared engine
json.type_persistence: Edits are full-build-hash-bound overlays replayed only in worker memory. The canonical project is not saved or mutated.

option_bags.backend: action=backups options.op (list, verify, remove: remove is a dry run unless confirm:true) and selectors; action=doctor options (sections, verbose)
option_bags.ghidra_query: type_edit options.kind (commit, commit_revert, rebase, publish, merge, export_bundle, import_bundle, plus today's kinds), options.view, options.expect_revision, options.as (the agent identity of the call, D59); status options.show (changes, views, lineage, queue, health)
option_bags.ghidra_run: options.isolation (private, shared, exclusive), options.readonly, options.as (the agent identity of the call, D59)
option_bags.job: status/cancel filters (kind, cid) for commit and backup jobs
option_bags.trace: per-action options: start (profile, images, scope, launch, program), query (kinds, filter, group_by, cursor, up_to, interpretation, profile_query), diff (against, group_by, align), explain (event_id, depth, direction), mark (label, phase), export (name, overwrite), check (assertions), import (input), resymbolize (program), reprocess (codecs, context|contexts, kinds, note), relations (op), evict (to_quota), bundle (path); start also takes meta fields (target, scenario, capture_options, shared_scope); writes use the cap that start returned; offline=true runs import/verify/rebuild/export on files; every action takes limit

observe/break.accept_patch: true: expect is the file's original prologue; a live detour another tool wrote is decoded, reported (patcher module) and probed past
observe/break.capture: up to 4 [{arg 0..7 under the convention, or reg (a register name; x64 xmm0..xmm15 hold float arguments: {reg: xmm2, as: f32}), deref?: [offsets: read a pointer at each], size?, as: utf8|utf16|hex|i8..u64|f32|f64|pointer|struct, fields? (struct), names? {value: name}, label?}]: bounded, range-checked copies decoded in the worker (events carry decoded)
observe/break.convention: native (default; x64 registers then stack, ia32 stack slots) | thiscall (32-bit: arg 0 = this in ecx) | fastcall (32-bit: ecx, edx, then stack)
observe/break.expect: exact live bytes before installing a probe
observe/break.instruction: true for a probe inside a function (no return hook; [sp] is not a return address there); automatic on x64 off a pdata function start
observe/break.sample: observe only: {window_s 1..300, capture: index of a numeric capture}: one summary per window (count, rate, min, max, last) instead of an event per call

patches.rows: [{module, rva, size?, name?}] 1..200: live vs file bytes, decoded detour and its module

read.address: absolute readable target address; mutually exclusive with module/rva
read.layout: optional [{name, offset, type, size?}]: decode the read as fields
read.module: exact loaded module name with rva, OR address for absolute heap/stack
read.target: the analysis target that defines type
read.type: optional type name from target's analysis (imported/overlay types) as the layout

spawn.cwd: optional absolute working directory (games resolve data relative to it)
spawn.env: optional {name: value} added to the caller's environment

writers.answer: which sites wrote object+offset in the window; a site too short for a probe is counted at its function's return sites; sites a jump lands in, or whose bytes hold a call, are refused with the reason
writers.target: analysis target (checks every site before probing)

json.semantics: Breakpoints capture observed registers, arguments and stack context; bounded automatic release prevents abandoned pauses. Detach removes instrumentation. CPU single-step is not supplied by this instrumentation backend.
json.setup: backend action=install component=runtime returns a job id; poll job status
json.trust: Every built-in probe requires module build identity and matching live bytes. Unrestricted injected scripts are not exposed because they could bypass that gate. No remote target or other MCP server is implied.
